_comment: Regression fixture for engine/eval_applicability.js (docs/product_roadmap.md M6, docs/milestone_log.md M6). Every case was run against the live evaluateRule() over the real data/derived/condition_bindings/*.json + data/pilots/*.json archive before being recorded here, following the same convention as test/fixtures/eval_questions.json's own stated rule. Regenerated after the completeness-gate + prompt fixes (docs/milestone_log.md M6 'binding pipeline hardening' entry) changed several bindings' bindability/verification_status — 11 of the original 29 cases' expected values changed, all traceable to specific, understood binding changes (e.g. a previously-loose predicate correctly reclassified non_bindable), none to an applicability.js bug. IMPORTANT: this fixture is agent-authored (the underlying bindings came from engine/binding_agent.js's automated pipeline, not human curation) — it is a regression fixture proving the engine is internally consistent and deterministic given its current binding data, NOT a human-verified golden ground truth that the bindings themselves are regulatorily correct (docs/product_roadmap.md §2.5.1's review_status distinction, applied to this derived layer). Do not hand-edit expected verdicts without re-running against the live engine. If EMA/FDA/S6 binding data is regenerated, this fixture must be regenerated too.

cases.note: binding cond.part1.3_3.002 is needs_review after the completeness-gate hardening (docs/milestone_log.md M6) — predicate holds but must not silently resolve to applicable
binding cond.part1.3_3.007 is needs_review (now binding_role=full_scope, still unverified) — predicate holds but must not silently resolve to applicable

cond.part1.3_3.007 is full_scope but needs_review, so a predicate mismatch is downgraded to unverified_binding rather than not_applicable — the same guard as a false full_scope would otherwise trigger

target_nature mismatch alone would be partial_scope_mismatch, but the binding's own needs_review status takes precedence for the predicate-holds-vs-not evaluation on the product_modality leaf

cond.part2.2_1.008 is now binding_role=full_scope AND verified (a real change from the prior partial_scope run) — a full_scope mismatch correctly produces not_applicable here, unlike the partial_scope cases elsewhere in this fixture
the boundary case that drove the binding_role design review — predicate false must never become not_applicable
cond.part2.2_1.004 is now binding_role=full_scope, still needs_review
